title: Penguin Parents Sleep 10,000 Times a Day, Four Seconds at a Time

scenes.text: A penguin parent falls asleep more than ten thousand times a day.
Scientists wired up fourteen chinstrap penguins in Antarctica and recorded their brains for two weeks.
Every nap lasted about four seconds. Add them up and it comes to over eleven hours of sleep.
Why? A nest on a crowded, noisy colony is never safe. Skuas are always watching for unguarded eggs and chicks.
So the penguin dozes, wakes, checks the sky, and dozes again, all day long.
Eleven hours of sleep, in ten thousand tiny pieces.

description:
A penguin parent falls asleep more than ten thousand times a day.
Chinstrap penguins on King George Island nap for about four seconds at a time, adding up to over eleven hours of sleep.
Could you sleep like that?
first_comment: Could you survive on four-second naps? Which animal should we look at next?
